recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-12401 unless the Pharmacy work group wants new optional example coverage beyond the Published DSTU2 application.
issue_request: FHIR-12401 was a Published FHIR-core Pharmacy change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking for MedicationRequest dosageInstruction examples using days of week and morning/noon/night or time-of-day style timing. The accepted resolution was to add representative examples for the related Timing changes from TR 12201, TR 12352, and TR 10478 and clarify occurrence/period-duration use.
initial_application: Jira comments report that the examples were added, and historical commit 8175cd268621dabb43c4f0dd0bf689fa0743e633 applied TR#12401 by adding medrx0333, medrx0334, and medrx0335 plus MedicationRequest examples metadata. Later source history refactored those examples for current Dosage and R5 MedicationRequest syntax while preserving the represented timing concepts.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is active in source/fhir.ini. Current medrx0333 uses Timing.repeat.when=MORN, medrx0334 uses Timing.repeat.dayOfWeek=mon with daily frequency/period, and medrx0335 uses Timing.repeat.timeOfDay=09:00:00; the current examples list and examples header include all three. FHIR-12460 addressed the linked Timing invariant problem that initially blocked such examples, while FHIR-12201, FHIR-12352, and FHIR-10478 are the Timing datatype changes the examples illustrate. Zulip and Confluence searches found no substantive conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source already satisfies the applied request with representative MedicationRequest examples, and adding more variants for every EventTiming code would be optional example expansion rather than a necessary correction.

related_jiras.note: Added Timing.repeat.dayOfWeek, which medrx0334 demonstrates in a MedicationRequest dosageInstruction.
Added Timing.repeat.timeOfDay, which medrx0335 demonstrates in a MedicationRequest dosageInstruction.
Added Morning/Afternoon/Evening/Night Timing.repeat.when codes, which medrx0333 demonstrates with MORN.
Loosened Timing invariants after the examples initially failed validation, supporting the current interpretation that these timing combinations are allowed.
